source_freeze.definition: source_rows_sha256 hashes every fetched row (all selected fields, in :id order, one JSON object per line). case_table_sha256 hashes the reduced case table in build order. Neither embeds the build timestamp, so a rebuild can be checked against them.
source_freeze.checked: The City republishes this dataset daily. At the time of construction the live total still summed to exactly 823,955 rows across the nine published case_disposition values, so no row was lost to paging and the freeze matches the source the checksums were taken from.

breakdown.detail: one COUNT(*) probe to read the published row total, then one request per 50,000-row page ordered by :id; the page count is recorded in the extract's build_summary.json

extraction_cost.machine_worker: 2 vCPU / 2 GB worker (cpx32, hel1), the gated construction run
extraction_cost.machine_rebuild: 4 vCPU / 1.9 GiB orchestration host, an independent rebuild of the same artifact
extraction_cost.method: the worker figure is the job's own elapsed_seconds for the whole container run (build plus qualification); the rebuild figure is wall clock around build.py alone, measured with resource.getrusage on a second machine

label_accounting.note: Rows, not cases: the published table is one row per violation charge, and one docket_number carries many rows. Only Liable and Not Liable carry the case-level signal; everything else is neither.

case_reduction.definition: A case ships when at least one of its charges carries a Liable or Not Liable disposition, its lead charge has a violation date and coordinates, and its notice date falls inside a declared split window. A case with some charges decided and some not is still labelled from the decided ones, so a case is a mixed-disposition case whenever any charge is neither Liable nor Not Liable - that is the normal case here, not the exception.

single_column_separation.method: each candidate feature was tested alone against the case-level label, as rank AUC over the built training split
single_column_separation.result: no shipped column separates the classes on its own: violation_date 0.502, ward 0.505, street_direction 0.508, street_type 0.503, distinct_code_count 0.565, charge_count 0.566
single_column_separation.rejected: an earlier version of this artifact shipped days_to_hearing, computed from the City's hearing_date. hearing_date is documented as 'the date of the most recent hearing', so for a decided case it is the hearing at which the disposition was recorded - after the prediction instant. days_to_hearing separated the classes on its own at AUC 0.8365. Both the column and everything derived from it were removed before this artifact was built and gated.

leakage_check.why_it_matters_here: The benchmark runner hands prediction code every column of a split that is not an identifier or the target, so a column that leaks cannot be left in place and documented away - it has to go.

duplicate_identifiers.note: docket_number is the case key and is unique in every shipped split; the split is taken over cases, so no case can appear in two periods.
